course_description:
Materials Characterisation provides unique tools for understanding the materials and their demonstrated properties. Materials Characterisation techniques, such as x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy, allow detailed structural, chemical, and morphological characteristics of materials to be determined, which has become essential tools for materials research and their productions. By correlating the determined structural and chemical characteristics of a material with its fabrication/processing, the formation mechanism of the material can be clarified. This is vital for developing new material systems, and for identifying problems in the production lines. On the other hand, the correlation of the determined structural and chemical characteristics of a material with its demonstrated properties allows the material's structure-property link to be built, which is critically important for understanding the origin of the properties. For this reason, demand for learning various materials characterization techniques have increased sharply in the recent decades.

With the rapid development of materials for their advanced applications, understanding the micro- and nano-structures of materials becomes critical for understanding the material’s properties and fabrication methods. This knowledge is essential for the design and development of future materials. This postgraduate course will provide students with advanced knowledge on a range of materials characterization instruments and associated techniques.

course_aims:
The course aims to:ﾠﾠ

(1)ﾠﾠﾠprovide students with aﾠdeep understandingﾠof advanced material characterization techniques, with a focus on crystallography, x-ray/diffraction and spectroscopy, electron diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy, as well as other advanced characterization techniques;ﾠand

(2)ﾠﾠﾠdevelop students' practical skills in selecting the best characterization tools/methods to determine the structural characteristics of target material system(s), and in scientific writing and presentation.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an understanding of characterization - Select the most appropriate characterization techniques (diffraction, microscopy and spectroscopy) to perform high-level materials characterization tasks
Demonstrate an understanding of characterization - Demonstrate expertise in operating characterization instruments for securing the best possible data

Demonstrate an understanding of characterization - Design experimental approach(es) to comprehensively determine the morphological, structural and chemical characteristics of complex materials tasks, in which multiple instruments and techniques may be employed
Perform diffraction characterizations skillfully - Describe crystal structures professionally by effective structure indexing
Perform diffraction characterizations skillfully - Estimate the microstructure features of materials based on X-ray diffraction data
Perform diffraction characterizations skillfully - Employ the electron diffraction technique to identify crystal structures
Perform diffraction characterizations skillfully - Identify the nature of crystals by modeling crystal structures and indexing electron diffraction patterns
Perform diffraction characterizations skillfully - Design diffraction experiments to effectively determine the structural characterisation of materials
Execute microscopic characterizations proficiently - Apply scanning electron microscopic techniques to determine the morphological characteristics of materials
Execute microscopic characterizations proficiently - Employ transmission electron microscopic techniques to determine the structural characteristics of materials
Execute microscopic characterizations proficiently - Determine the structural and chemical characteristics of materials using scanning transmission electron microscopy
Execute microscopic characterizations proficiently - Design microscopic experiments to effectively clarify the microstructures of materials
Implement spectroscopic characterizations expertly - Employ the X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy to determine the chemical characteristics of materials
Implement spectroscopic characterizations expertly - Establish the bonding and chemical characteristics of materials using electron energy loss spectroscopy
Implement spectroscopic characterizations expertly - Determine the bonding and chemical characteristics of material surfaces using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and X-ray fluorescence

Implement spectroscopic characterizations expertly - Understand the principles and applications of other advanced characterisation techniques, such as Auger electron spectroscopy and secondary-ion mass spectroscopy
Implement spectroscopic characterizations expertly - Design spectroscopic experiments to effectively determine the bonding and chemical characteristics of materials and/or their surfaces
Communicate professionally - Employ the norms of the discipline to describe the outcomes of experimental investigations and other explorations into materials characterization
Communicate professionally - Present research outcomes by critically evaluating and logically presenting the relevant tasks
Communicate professionally - Contribute to team work in practical groups through data analysis and materials characterization.

assessment_details.task_description: Throughout the course, students will complete five exercises in Weeks 4, 5, 6, 7 and 13. Each exercise is worth 5 marks in the final mark. Each exercise contains a set of questions and students need to apply the knowledge learnt from the lectures to provide the best solutions to the questions. Students' answers will be marked based on the correctness. Week 4: Crystal structure Students will apply the learned knowledge from Lecture 3 and analyse given problems to provide the best solutions. Answers must be submitted through TurnItIn at end of the session (21/08/2026 3:00 pm) Week 5: Diffraction Students will apply the learned knowledge from Lectures 3 and 4 and analyse given problems to provide the best solutions. Answers must be submitted through TurnItIn at end of the session (28/08/2026 3:00 pm). Week 6: Indexing of electron diffraction patterns Students will apply the fundamental knowledge of electron diffraction, combined with knowledge of the forbidden rule of reflections and relationships between atomic planes and zone-axis, and analyse given questions to correctly index electron diffraction patterns. Answers must be submitted through TurnItIn at end of the session (4/09/2026 3:00 pm) Week 7: Crystal structure modelling In this practical, students will build the structural models of 7 material systems, in which students are required to provide their bonding natures. Students will have one week to complete the work. Answers must be submitted through TurnItIn by 18/09/2026 12:00 pm. Week 13: XPS Students will apply the learnt knowledge from Lecture 10 and analyse given problems to provide the best solutions. The task is divided into 5 stages, namely: Stage 1 – XPS examination of the surface coating of the ‘as-received’ Stock Nanomaterial. Stage 2 – XPS examination of the Stock Nanomaterial after Piranha Treatment to clean and hydroxylate the surface in preparation for the attachment on the initiator. Stage 3 – XPS examination of the stock Nanomaterial after attachment of the initiator. Stage 4 – XPS examination the monomer OEGMA – Oligo Ethylene Glycol MethAcrylate. Stage 5 – XPS examination after the Atom Transfer Radical Polymerisation to produce the Poly OEGMA ‘brush’. Answers must be submitted through TurnItIn at end of the session (30/10/2026 3:00 pm). Please refer to Blackboard for a detailed marking criteria. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Materials characterization
assessment_details.task_description: In this project, students will gain practical experience in comprehensively performing advanced characterization of a known material by characterizing it using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopic (SEM) techniques, namely secondary electrons (SE), backscattered electrons (BSE), and X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS). In this Practical, 4 alloys (namely 1090 plain carbon steel, AZ91 magnesium alloy, Ti6Al4V titanium alloy and high chromium white cast iron) will be investigated. Students will be divided into four groups, and each group will be given two samples of the same alloy. Attendance at your allocated practical sessions is compulsory unless you have received extension approval from the School of Mechanical and Mining Engineering. Failure to attend the practical classes without approval will result in a reduction in the final mark for the report in accordance with the marking criteria. Based on the obtained experimental results and critical analysis, students are required to determine the nature of your samples and draw comprehensive conclusions of experimental finding. Please note: Although the practical will be done in groups, students MUST write individual reports. This means that students write the reports by their own using the results from the group practical. Please refer to Blackboard for a detailed marking criteria. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task.
